properties.description: Anthony's word, 2026-09-12 ("go with your recommendation for 1 and 2" — item 2). A root-cause fix of the defect recorded the same day as fact:plan-epoch-on-an-existing-epoch-resets-its-status-to-planned: the core `plan_epoch` sets `status: planned` on every call, so the constructor's own revise path (same id, new prose) put an ARRIVED epoch back to planned, and every arrival of increments 430–434 needed a second set_epoch_status. IN: the core constructor sets `planned` only when the epoch does not yet exist; a revise leaves status alone (BL-183's discipline on a second type); a handler test shown to fail first; the defect fact closed with a valid_to and the change event recorded as a corrected cause. NOT IN: anything else about epochs.
properties.name: Increment 439 — revising an epoch's prose keeps its status
